data.title: Paramount Skydance (NASDAQ:PSKY) Stock Slides as Paramount Keeps Major DC Components
data.description:
Entertainment giant Paramount Skydance (PSKY)—soon to be just "Skydance"—had its share of outstanding questions going forward from the merger with Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD). That merger has not happened yet, but should be finished in the next few days. One of those outstanding questions focused on the DC Studios operation, and has now been resolved. This good news was not good enough for investors, though, as shares slipped modestly in the closing minutes of Friday's trading. Paramount has seen a 51.07% loss in its share price over the past year.

Still In and Swinging

The big question for Paramount and DC Studios came down to whether or not they would get rid of James Gunn and Peter Safran, the current heads of DC Studios. And even as Paramount is cleaning house, this was a part it decided not to touch, leaving both Gunn and Safran in to run the combination film, television, and comic book operation, according to a report from Deadline.

Gunn has already been hard at work getting Clayface ready for its October 23 release, and the Superman sequel, Man of Tomorrow, ready for July 9, 2027. Given that Superman was Warner's second-highest-grossing film at over $618 million, there is every reason to let Gunn cook. And it seems like Paramount seems inclined to do exactly that.

Taking Inventory

A point that has emerged in the comments sections on these articles often wonders what Paramount will actually do next. Especially given the new moves it has made, like bringing in Ynon Kreiz to serve as co-CEO. Kriez had a lot of impact on Mattel (MAT) with the Barbie movie, but what will he look into first at Paramount?

He will have no shortage of fodder to work with here. There is the Star Trek series, of course, which has seen better days, but still represents a long-term money-maker with piles of name recognition. It has every property from Adult Swim to work with, the entirety of DC Studios—as mentioned previously—everything in the Discovery Family Channel, Nickelodeon, and plenty more besides. It will also have New Line Cinema, which means that it will likely have two Nightmare on Elm Street titles coming out soon.

data.title: GameStop (GME) CEO Ryan Cohen Buys $10 Million of Company Stock
data.description:
GameStop (GME) CEO Ryan Cohen continues to load up on shares of the company he runs. Regulatory filings show that Cohen bought 450,000 shares of GME stock for $10.6 million on Sept. 29, bringing his direct holdings to just over 40.9 million shares, a stake worth $998.36 million or 8% of the video game retailer.

The purchase on Sept. 29 was Cohen's third major buy of GME stock in less than a month. The CEO acquired $20.4 million worth of shares on Sept. 10 and an additional $26.3 million of company stock on Sept. 21. Other members of senior management have also been buying GameStop's stock. On Oct. 1, Nat Turner, who sits on the company's board of directors, bought 10,462 shares for $24.33 apiece, bringing his purchase to $252,238.

Alignment with Stockholders

Why Cohen has been loading up on GME stock isn't clear. However, earlier this year, he said that it is important for chief executive officer's of public companies to buy stock with their personal funds "in order to further strengthen alignment with stockholders." Many other CEOs purchase company stock for the same reasons, including Greg Abel, the CEO of Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B).

data.title: Ford Stock (NYSE:F) Sinks as it Keeps Number 3 Sales Position in the Third Quarter
data.description:
Good news, of a sort, arrived for legacy automaker Ford (F). A report from CNBC noted that Ford managed to hold on to its position as the third-largest seller of vehicles in the United States. This turned out to be much closer than expected, as Ford nearly dropped to number four behind Hyundai Motor (HYMLF). That near-miss cost Ford, though, as investors dealt Ford shares a fractional loss in Friday afternoon's trading. Ford has also seen a 3.16% loss in its share price over the past year.

Pronounced Sales Drop

Ford reported that it turned in a sales decline of 6.6% for the third quarter, posting a grand total of 507,395 light-duty vehicles sold. This does not include heavy-duty vehicle sales, the report noted, as those are considered under different figures. But this figure, as disappointing as it might have been, still managed to succeed against Hyundai, who posted 506,200 vehicles sold in the quarter. This was up 5.4% against the previous year's third quarter, the report noted.

Last week, Cox Automotive posted a forecast that said Hyundai would outsell Ford this quarter, which would have been the first time such a thing had happened. But thanks to that narrow win, Ford managed to hold its position in the top three of sales. Ford, for its part, noted that this has been an unusual year, as it faced several out-of-the-ordinary supply chain issues and discontinued some of its biggest sellers, like the Ford Escape. This point is not lost on those who said that it was a bad idea to stop selling the Escape to begin with.

A Solar Win

Meanwhile, Ford picked up a bit of a win for green technology, as it will tap into a new installation recently finished in Coldwater, Michigan. The 100-megawatt Cold Creek Solar Park was recently put in place by DTE Energy (DTE), and the power that park generates will in part go into Ford's operations. Ford, for its part, agreed to buy as much as 650 MW of renewable energy from DTE via the CleanVision MIGreenPower program.

Ford still plans to make every Ford vehicle assembled in Michigan assembled with "…the equivalent of carbon-free electricity…" before 2027 ends, noted a report from Solar Power World.

data.title: American Airlines (AAL) Lets Customers Mix Cash and Miles to Buy Tickets
data.description:
American Airlines (AAL) has announced a new plan that allows customers to buy tickets for flights using a combination of cash and miles. The change comes as the carrier tries to grow its lucrative loyalty rewards program. The Texas-based company said that, going forward, its customers will see a slider bar allowing them to combine AAdvantage program miles with cash for tickets purchases at checkout.

The option to combine cash and rewards could be useful when people don't have enough miles in their account to cover the entire ticket and are looking to shave some cash off the ticket price. Competing airlines, including United (UAL) and Delta (DAL) already allow their customers to combine frequent flyer miles with cash to make purchases.

How Combo Purchases Work

For example, a one-way ticket on United from its Newark Liberty International Airport hub in New Jersey to Paris the first week of November was going for 40,000 United MileagePlus miles plus $5.60 in tax, $428.50 in cash, or $369 plus 6,000 miles.

data.title: Dow Jones Today: DJIA Advances as Jobs Report Miss Sends Rate Hike Odds Lower
data.description:
The Dow Jones (DJIA) is up 0.42% on Friday after a weak jobs report sent rate hike odds lower. In September, the U.S. economy added 29,000 nonfarm payrolls, well below the estimate of 84,000. Private payrolls rose by 46,000, while government employment fell by 17,000. Furthermore, the unemployment rate increased to 4.2% from 4.1%, topping expectations of 4.1%. The rate rose to 4.18% from 4.14% on an unrounded basis.

Following the report, the odds of a 25-basis-point hike at the October 28 Fed meeting dipped to 21.6% from 24.4% on Thursday and 64.2% a week ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool. In addition, the odds of unchanged rates rose to 78.4% from 75.6% a day ago and 35.8% a week ago.

Steady rates are generally viewed as more accretive to stocks than higher rates. Lower, rather than higher, rates allow companies to borrow capital more easily and can encourage hiring. In addition, lower rates increase the present value of discounted future cash flows.

data.title: Oil Ticks Higher Despite G7's 100 Million-Barrel Release
data.description:
Brent crude (BZ), the global oil benchmark, is up 0.51% to $102.82 per barrel, shrugging off news that member countries in the Group of Seven (G7) agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of oil from reserves. The announcement initially sent prices lower, although concerns over tight global supply and geopolitical risks later reversed the move.

G7 said the release will take place over four months, with a "substantial diesel release within the first 20 days." In March, the group agreed to release 400 million barrels.

Oil Prices Surge 32% Since Start of U.S.-Iran War

Oil prices have surged since the onset of the U.S.-Iran war and are up by 32% since late February. Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz has pushed prices higher, as the waterway handles roughly 20% of global oil flows.

data.title: Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) Week in Review: Quantum Pains, PC Gains
data.description:
This was a pretty big week for chip stock Intel (INTC). We discovered how far Intel was going with its ambitions in quantum computing, which turned out to be not very far at all. Changing economics and the brass tacks of Intel's foundry moves also weighed on the stock. Investors seem mildly concerned about Intel's overall fate, as Intel dropped fractionally in Friday afternoon's trading. Intel has seen a 225.82% rally in its share price over the past year.

The Skeleton Quantum Crew

Intel revealed that it had 70 people working on quantum computing, a move that, at the time, sent Intel share prices slumping hard. Intel was working on "silicon spin qubits," which could represent a huge step forward for Intel, particularly if it could get those qubits made in Intel's current factories. Despite CEO Lip-Bu Tan noting that quantum was a part of Intel's plan for the next five to 10 years, the fact that it only had 70 people working on quantum left investors deeply concerned.

Competitors are Partners

Intel advanced a strange notion on Tuesday, revealing that it considered its competitors to be more like partners. Intel's CEO told a story about how closely connected to Nvidia (NVDA) he was, and how Nvidia stepped in to offer investment when Lip-Bu Tan was CEO of Cadence Design Systems (CDNS).

Promotion

NVDS: built for a short position on NVDA

This was good enough for investors at the time, who gave Intel a slight boost in share prices. And indeed, considering how many of those competitors are making purchases from Intel on a regular basis—chances are not all of Nvidia's computers are AMD (AMD) powered—Intel's competitors are often customers as well.

Foundry Financing

Then, Intel found it may have had an issue with its foundry financing. It managed to find partners to help get it up and running—good news for Intel's cash on hand—but the partnership came with conditions that would prove tough for Intel. Agreements covering production rates and inventory rates mean that Intel will have to sell much of what it makes, and as quickly as possible.

A Shifting Picture

Finally, Intel's week wrapped up on an oddly speculative note, as Intel's financial picture went from one of survival to one of expansion. Intel's finances a few months ago were focused on keeping the company intact. Cost cuts, layoffs, reduced management and more all added up to money not spent.

Intel expanding its production lines comes at a time when Intel's market for chips is on the rise as well. This is about the best possible situation for Intel right now, especially given earlier reports that Intel needs to sell just about everything it produces as part of the terms of its recent partnership efforts.

data.title: Nvidia Stock (NVDA) Hits All-Time High Days After Announcing Record Buyback
data.description:
The stock of chipmaker Nvidia (NVDA) has hit an all-time high on Oct. 2, days after the company increased its current stock buyback authorization by a record $150 billion. At noon hour, NVDA stock was up 2% on the day and changing hands at an all-time high of $237.88 per share. Nvidia's market capitalization now stands at $5.67 trillion, making it the world's most valuable publicly traded company.

Despite hitting a new all-time high, NVDA stock continues to lag behind stocks of other microchip makers whose processors are used in the artificial intelligence (AI) buildout. Year-to-date, NVDA stock is up 25%. While decent, that gain is modest compared to rivals such as Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) whose stock has risen 182% so far in 2026.
data.author: Joel Baglole

data.title: Storage Stocks WDC and STX Sink 11% — Here's Why Morgan Stanley Says It Would 'Gladly' Buy the Dip
data.description:
Shares in leading data storage manufacturers Western Digital (WDC) and Seagate (STX) fell by 11% on Friday afternoon. This followed reports that Japanese tech giant Toshiba plans to commit about $380 million to double its capacity to produce hard disk drives (HDD) used in AI data centers. In response, Morgan Stanley (MS) pushed back against the fear, noting that even with Toshiba's move, the supply-demand balance will stay tight through 2028. As a result, the banking giant will "gladly buy STX/WDC on this dip."

data.title: Cycurion Stock (CYCU) Soars 48% After Regaining Nasdaq Compliance
data.description:
Cycurion (CYCU) stock surged 48.33% higher on Friday after the AI-driven cybersecurity company announced it is no longer in immediate danger of being delisted. The company said it has regained compliance with the Nasdaq (NDAQ)'s minimum bid price rule. It received a letter from the Nasdaq's Hearings Office dated October 1 that confirmed that Cycurion met the $1.00 minimum bid price rule. Its stock continues to trade on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the CYCU ticker.

Cycurion took action to fix the CYCU stock price issue in August. On August 28, the company carried out a one-for-eight reverse stock split. Since then, its bid price has closed above $1.00 for 10 straight trading days. The Nasdaq's compliance review confirmed that the company met the price test set by the Hearings Panel.

The Nasdaq Hearings Panel had given Cycurion more time to meet the rule in a September 9 decision. The company had to show that it met the bid price test by September 11. The October 1 letter confirmed that this condition was met. As a result, Cycurion can keep trading on the Nasdaq.
